results.title: Review Findings from Ethical Reviews of Non-Medical Research in ...
results.content: This study examined how ethical reviews are actually conducted in non-medical research in Japan through an analysis of 70 review comments on 19 proposals reviewed by the ethics committee of University A in 2015, using the qualitative method SCAT (Steps for Coding and Theorization). Therefore, this study aims to concretely understand the actual practices of ethical review in non-medical research by closely analyzing the review comments issued by one university’s ethics committee, which cooperated with the study. This study analyzed the review comments for all 19 non-medical research proposals newly reviewed in 2015 by the ethics committee of University A in Japan. In order to understand the actual practice of ethical review in non-medical research at a practical level, this study closely examined the content of review comments that were actually issued. This study analyzed the actual review comments from a university ethics committee to clarify how ethical reviews are conducted in non-medical research.

results.title: Ethical Consideration in R&D R&D NIPPON SHINYAKU CO., LTD.
results.content: ## Ethical consideration in basic research using human-derived samples. To treat those who provide such samples or information in an ethically responsible and considerate manner, we at Nippon Shinyaku have taken necessary measures, notably the establishment of in-house regulations based on the research ethics guidelines set by the Japanese Government (including the Ethical Guidelines for Medical and Health Research Involving Human Subjects), and the formation of a research ethics committee comprising members from both within and outside the company to conduct a fair, neutral, and rigorous examination of the ethical validity and scientific rationality of the company’s R&D.\*1. While using human-derived samples and information on human health in research, Nippon Shinyaku obtains prior consent from those who provide such samples and information (research participants), in compliance with the related laws, regulations, and research ethics guidelines.

results.title: The Current Status and Future Direction of Clinical Research in ...
results.content: Although stakeholders such as researchers, medical institutions, and pharmaceutical companies that conduct interventional research are required to understand and appropriately comply with this Act, it is believed that there is still room for making further improvements in the Act. As the Clinical Trials Act was originally created for purpose of restoring trust in the clinical research conducted in Japan after several scandals, it requires bigger changes and more careful handling to be carried out by stakeholders, such as medical institutions and pharmaceutical companies than those required under the regulations stipulated by the existing ethical guidelines. Therefore, currently, the clinical interventional research that receives funding from a company and similar studies fall under the Clinical Trials Act (6) and all other clinical research falls under the Ethical Guidelines for Medical and Biological Research Involving Human Subjects (9). 5. Current issues, future direction, and effort toward revising the Clinical Trials Act. As little time has passed since the establishment of the Ethical Guidelines for Medical and Biological Research Involving Human Subjects, the issues with these guidelines have yet to be clearly identified.
